articles.title: Your Critical Vulnerabilities Might Not Be Your Biggest Risk
articles.summary: Security teams have become exceptionally talented at finding vulnerabilities. Now, it’s time to turn our attention to optimizing the process for determining which of those vulnerabilities actually create a path to compromise.   A critical vulnerability may look alarming on a scanner report, but if it sits behind strong segmentation, identity controls, and other defenses that prevent an attacker from reaching anything important, then it doesn’t necessarily need immediate attention.    On the other hand, a medium-severity vulnerability may appear less important, but if it can be used to provide a foothold that can be chained with other weaknesses to reach sensitive data or privileged systems, then fixing that gap becomes a priority.   How Autonomous Penetration Testing Reveals What Attackers Can Actually Exploit   Severity scores tell you what vulnerabilities could mean in isolation. Autonomous penetration testing  tells you what an attacker can actually do with the vulnerabilities....
articles.title_fr: Vos vulnérabilités critiques pourraient ne pas être votre plus grand risque
articles.summary_fr: Les équipes de sécurité sont douées pour trouver des vulnérabilités, mais il est crucial d'optimiser le processus pour déterminer lesquelles mènent réellement à une compromission. Une vulnérabilité critique bien protégée peut être moins urgente qu'une vulnérabilité de gravité moyenne qui, combinée à d'autres faiblesses, permet d'atteindre des données sensibles. Les tests d'intrusion autonomes révèlent ce que les attaquants peuvent réellement exploiter, au-delà des scores de gravité isolés.

articles.title: Attackers Chain JFrog Artifactory Flaws to Gain Admin Control and Plant Backdoors
articles.summary: Attackers have chained two flaws in JFrog Artifactory , the repository that software build pipelines pull from, to take administrator control of self-hosted servers and plant backdoors, cloud security company Wiz said in a report.   Wiz saw the attacks between August 15 and September 8. JFrog had fixed both flaws before then, so only servers that had not been updated were open to them.   Neither flaw gives administrator control on its own.      CVE-2026-42018 makes Artifactory hand an internal anonymous-user token to a caller who has not logged in, even when anonymous access is turned off.    CVE-2026-42016  then allows that low-privilege token to be swapped for one with administrator scope, because Artifactory checks a token's signature and who issued it, but not what the token is allowed to do. articles.title_fr: Des attaquants enchaînent des failles de JFrog Artifactory pour obtenir un contrôle administrateur et implanter des portes dérobées
articles.summary_fr: Des attaquants ont exploité deux failles en chaîne dans JFrog Artifactory pour prendre le contrôle administrateur de serveurs auto-hébergés et y implanter des portes dérobées, selon Wiz. articles.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor
articles.summary: A China-linked hacking group exploited a flaw in Sogou Input Method , one of the most widely used tools for typing Chinese characters on Windows, to install a backdoor on victims' computers, security company Gen Digital said in  research published Thursday .   The attack started with a crafted link and ended with the attacker able to do anything the logged-in user could do. Tencent, which owns and develops Sogou, fixed the flaw in April 2026.   Gen found the flaw while investigating a live intrusion by UNC3569 , a group that  Google Threat Intelligence ties to China  and places in the country's hacker-for-hire scene. Google has tracked the group since 2021 and says it has targeted government, education, technology, and finance sectors, mostly in East and Southeast Asia.   The backdoor it installed is GRAYRABBIT , a small program the group has used for years and that Google describes as its first step onto a machine.
